short: Whole-word output (M08) is new only to intracranial recordings (Suppes 1997, EEG/MEG); DTW kernel (M06) gain unshown; imagery window confounded by heard and upcoming overt word.
position: Both changed components are standard when judged over any signal, as in the published Martin 2014 review [@martin2016word]. Whole-word output (M08) is new to intracranial recordings, where none of 4 earlier decoders classifies words (Appendix), but Suppes et al. recognised single internal-speech word trials from scalp EEG/MEG in 1997 [@suppes1997brain]. DTW inside the SVM kernel (M06) is new to neural decoding but was used for acoustic words [@wan2005polynomial] and silent-speech EMG [@freitas2012towards], and its gain has no stated unit and no per-subject result. The test partition (M12) is the usual within-participant cross-validation. The protocol cannot attribute the result to imagery: the 1.5 s window sits between hearing a word and repeating it aloud, with no control epoch [@martin2016word]. The claim of "the first demonstration of single-trial neural decoding of words during imagined speech production" fails on scope and task: subjects imagined hearing, not saying [@martin2016word].
